newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech government subsidises flood loans to firms.
newsitem.headline: Czech government subsidises flood loans to firms.

text.p: The Czech government approved one billion crowns of additional funds from the state budget to subsidise low-interest reconstruction loans for firms damaged by July's floods, Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl said on Friday.

He told reporters the funds would be administered through the state-controlled development bank Ceskomoravska Zarucni a Rozvojova Banka and were intended to subsidise interest rates on credits totalling 15 to 18 billion crowns.
Kuhnl said the programme to subsidise loans was necessary because of the current level of Czech commercial interest rates, which are hovering well above 15 percent.
"We would like to see interest rates reduced but it of course depends on the fiscal and monetary situation in the Czech Republic," the minister said.
"The main reason why we started this (reconstruction) programme was exactly the high level of interest rates."
Kuhnl did not say what interest rates would be paid by businesses drawing money from the subsidies programme.

The Czech government on Wednesday approved 1.9 billion crowns from the state budget to help pay for communication and ecological problems caused by the flooding and is to request some 2.3 billion crowns in aid from the European Union through its PHARE programme.
It had already approved the issuance of five billion crowns in flood-relief bonds, and assigned around five billion crowns out of privatisation proceeds to the afflicted areas.
It is also considering a loan of more than 10 billion crowns from the European Investment Bank.
Still, ministers have said a special flood relief tax might be considered to help cover costs of the reconstruction.
Total flood damage in the Czech Republic has been estimated at 60 billion crowns. -- Pavel Novak +420-2-2423-0003
